linkedin.content:
Lexical data is rarely just “put these rows in a database.”

The risky part is what happens when source files disagree: fields drift, glosses mix languages, some entries are incomplete, and a convenient cleanup can erase where a reading came from.

I built a small synthetic proof that keeps raw fields, locators and hashes, stores gloss normalization separately, quarantines incomplete records, and makes zero writes on an identical replay. An injected failure leaves every ingestion table empty.

The page explains the design and links the runnable Python/SQLite sample:
https://lazying.art/lkt/lexical-ingest/?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=lexical_data_carpentry&utm_content=proof

It is a workflow sample, not a compatibility or linguistic-accuracy claim.
